title: Phone Calls
tagline: Phone calls: bad lines, questions, what you're doing, and saying goodbye.
canDo: You can hold a whole phone call with family in Pakistan

grammar.title: Question words
grammar.body: kya (what), kab (when), kahan (where), kaun (who), kyun (why), kaise (how). They usually sit right before the verb: 'aap kahan hain?' 'aap kab aa rahe hain?' Kya at the very start turns a sentence into a yes/no question.

grammar.title: Present continuous: -raha hoon
grammar.body: Stem + raha/rahi/rahe + hoon/ho/hai/hain. main parh raha hoon (I'm studying, man), main parh rahi hoon (woman), aap kya kar rahe hain? (respectful). In speech the final hai is often dropped: 'awaaz nahin aa rahi'.

teach.title: -raha hoon = I'm …ing
teach.info: Verb stem + raha/rahi/rahe + hoon/hai/hain. 'Main khana bana raha hoon' = I'm making food. Raha for a man, rahi for a woman, rahe for aap or plural.

teach.tip: Parhna = to study / read. Every parent's favourite verb.
